In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the isovector properties of nuclear matter are very sensitive to the nuclear interactions used, but the isospin dependence of the nucleon mean field in asymmetric nuclear matter is not very sensitive to the details of the nuclear interactions.

the empirical constraints on the symmetry energy and the isospinsplitting of the effective nucleon mass in isospinsymmetric nuclear matter are satisfied by most of the parameter sets in the nonlinear relativistic mean-field theory, while only a few parameter sets in the density-dependent relativistic mean-field theories and the point-coupling relativistic mean-field approach can reproduce the empirical constraints on both the symmetry energy and isospin splitting.

the empirical constraints from isospin diffusion, isotopic scaling, and giant monopole resonance measurements are not yet strong enough to rule out the majority of the parameter sets in the widely used relativistic mean-field theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isospin properties of asymmetric nuclear matters are sensitive to the choice of nuclear interactions and the definition of the optical potential.
the isospin dependence of the nucleon single-particle potential is not well determined by nuclear structure data alone.

a relativistic mean-field description of asymmetric nuclear matter is not yet well established, and that more work is needed to improve our understanding of the properties of neutron-rich nuclear matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
one needs to be very careful when using the nuclear symmetry energy to constrain the nuclear interaction in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter.

, for the nuclear models to be used in heavy-ion reaction studies, it is important to ensure that their predictions for nuclear symmetry energy and the nuclear symmetry potential are consistent with the constraints extracted from the experimental data.

, in order to make reliable predictions for the isospin dependence of the nucleon mean free path, transport coefficients, and the nucleon effective masses in neutron-rich nuclear systems, it is essential to have a good understanding of the nuclear symmetry energy and its density dependence, and to be aware of the possible ambiguities due to the different definitions of the nucleon single-particle potential in asymmetric nuclear matter.
